title: Festivals around the world

items: Festival | Who celebrates | What it marks
Diwali | Hindus, Sikhs, Jains | Light over darkness
Eid al-Fitr | Muslims | The end of Ramadan
Christmas | Christians | The birth of Jesus
Lunar New Year | China, Korea, Vietnam and more | A new year begins

explain.say: Festivals are special days when people celebrate together, remember an important story, and share food, gifts and prayers. Let's visit five festivals celebrated around the world.

Diwali, in October or November, is the festival of lights. Families light little clay lamps called diyas, share sweets and enjoy fireworks. Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita coming home, Sikhs remember Guru Hargobind's release, and Jains remember Mahavira.

draw.text: Diyas, rangoli patterns, sweets and new clothes.

explain.say: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan, the month when Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. People pray together, wear new clothes, give to the poor, and visit family, saying Eid Mubarak, which means blessed Eid. A second festival, Eid al-Adha, comes during the Hajj.

Christmas, on the 25th of December for most Christians, celebrates the birth of Jesus. People go to church, sing carols, decorate trees and give presents. Hanukkah is the Jewish festival of eight nights, when one more candle is lit each night on the menorah.

Lunar New Year, also called Spring Festival, starts the new year on the moon calendar, between late January and mid-February. Families gather for a big reunion dinner, give red envelopes with money, and watch lion and dragon dances. Each year is named after one of twelve animals.

draw.text: Then Horse, Goat, Monkey, Rooster, Dog and Pig: twelve animals in all.

explain.say: Every festival is different, but look at what they share: special food, family and friends, light or decoration, giving to others, and a story that matters. Which festivals does your family celebrate?

items: Gifts and help for people in need

faq.a: Diwali is the festival of lights, celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains in October or November. It celebrates light over darkness and good over evil. Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita returning home and pray to the goddess Lakshmi; Sikhs remember Guru Hargobind's release from prison; Jains remember Mahavira.

At Eid al-Fitr, which ends the month of Ramadan, Muslims go to the mosque for special prayers, give charity so the poor can celebrate too, wear new clothes, visit family and share delicious food. People greet each other with Eid Mubarak, meaning blessed Eid.

faq.q: What is the difference between the two Eids?
faq.a: Eid al-Fitr, the festival of breaking the fast, comes at the end of Ramadan. Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice, comes during the Hajj and remembers the Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to obey God; families often share meat with relatives, neighbours and people in need.

faq.q: Why does Eid change date every year?
faq.a: The Islamic calendar follows the moon, and its year is about 11 days shorter than the usual calendar year. So Eid comes about 11 days earlier each year, slowly moving through all the seasons. Many Muslims wait to see the new crescent moon to know the day.
asks: why is Eid on a different day

faq.a: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, when Muslims who are able fast from dawn until sunset, with no food or drink in daylight. It is a time of prayer, reading the Qur'an, kindness and charity. Children, the sick, the elderly and travellers do not have to fast.

Lunar New Year, also called Chinese New Year or Spring Festival, begins the new year on the lunar calendar, between late January and mid-February. It is celebrated in China, Korea, Vietnam and by communities worldwide, with family reunion dinners, red envelopes, firecrackers, and lion and dragon dances.
asks: how is Lunar New Year celebrated

faq.q: Why are there animals for each year?
faq.a: The Chinese zodiac names each year after one of twelve animals, in order: Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Goat, Monkey, Rooster, Dog and Pig. A folk story tells of a great race the animals ran, and the order they finished in.

faq.q: Why do people give red envelopes?
faq.a: At Lunar New Year, adults give children and unmarried relatives red envelopes with money inside. Red stands for luck and happiness in Chinese culture, so the gift is a wish for good fortune in the new year.
asks: why red at Chinese New Year

faq.a: Christmas is the Christian festival celebrating the birth of Jesus, on the 25th of December for most Christians and the 7th of January for many Orthodox Christians. People go to church, sing carols, act out the nativity story, decorate trees and give gifts.

Hanukkah is a Jewish festival of eight nights, usually in December. It remembers the Temple in Jerusalem being rededicated long ago, and the story of a little oil that burned for eight days. Each night families light one more candle on the menorah, eat fried treats and play dreidel.
asks: what do Jewish people celebrate in December

faq.a: There are many more. Hindus celebrate Holi, the festival of colours, in spring; Christians celebrate Easter; Jews celebrate Passover, remembering freedom from Egypt; Sikhs celebrate Vaisakhi; and Buddhists celebrate Vesak, remembering the Buddha's life.

Holi is the Hindu festival of colours, held in spring. People throw coloured powder and water at each other, dance and share sweets. It celebrates the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil, remembered in the story of Prahlad.
asks: why do people throw colours at Holi

faq.q: Can you celebrate a festival from another religion?
faq.a: Many festivals welcome guests: friends of all faiths join Diwali parties, Eid meals, Christmas carols and Lunar New Year parades. Being a respectful guest, asking about the meaning, and joining in the food and fun is a great way to learn about your neighbours.
asks: celebrating with friends of other faiths

facts: Diwali is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains, usually in October or November.
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan, the Islamic month of fasting from dawn to sunset.
The Islamic year is about 11 days shorter than the solar year, so Eid moves earlier each year.
Hanukkah lasts eight nights, and its menorah has nine branches including the helper candle, the shamash.
Lunar New Year falls between late January and mid-February, and each year is named after one of twelve animals.

quiz.why: Eid al-Fitr, the festival of breaking the fast, comes at the end of Ramadan.

quiz.say: Apply. A family eats a big reunion dinner, gives children red envelopes and watches a dragon dance. Which festival is it?
quiz.show: Reunion dinner, red envelopes, dragon dance: which festival?
quiz.why: Reunion dinners, red envelopes for luck and lion and dragon dances are Lunar New Year traditions.

wrong.0: Christmas has trees, carols and presents, but not red envelopes and dragon dances.
wrong.2: Eid al-Adha is a Muslim festival during the Hajj, when families share meat with others.
